message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's most recent results and placed one order: a buy of **44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.90**, which filled at $222.90 for a total of **$9,807.60** — inside your $10,000 per-order cap and well under the $20,000 daily limit, with the limit set only ~0.1% above the $222.70 market quote (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72). My decision relied on Apple's FQ4 2024 release (quarter ended 9/28/2024, announced 10/31/2024): quarterly revenue of **$94.9 billion, up 6% year over year**, and FY2024 total net sales of **$391,035 million**, net income of **$93,736 million**, diluted EPS of **$6.08** (including a one-time $10.2 billion tax charge), and operating income of **$123,216 million**, all confirmed from Apple Newsroom and the SEC EDGAR 10-K. I explicitly discarded a third-party "filings mirror" page that reported FY2024 revenue of $361.2 billion, net income of $79.4 billion, and EPS of $5.12, since those figures contradict the primary filings. The thesis is a return to revenue growth plus a services/buyback-supported multiple and the Apple Intelligence/iPhone 16 upgrade cycle ahead, against the risk of a rich ~36x trailing P/E; I sized the position conservatively rather than committing the full daily budget, and I did not touch your existing MSFT position or withdraw any funds.
